Delivery epic: downstream Batter applications stop hand-rolling feature flags from environment variables and declare typed flags and kill switches once, in code.

Canonical plan: `.agent/plans/flags-control-plane.md` (Critical profile, proposed 2026-11-04, repository baseline fb83054). It is a gitignored file in the checkout of the design session's machine; the child beads carry their own task text, and §4 (design) lives only in that file. Status: proposed; ADR-016 acceptance by the owner (T-01) is the first gate.

## 1. Outcome

Downstream Batter applications stop hand-rolling feature flags from environment variables.
They declare every flag and kill switch once, in code, as typed handles in one catalog, and
evaluate them only through those handles. Work evaluates through one view per HTTP request, job
invocation or periodic run; the application may pin a decision into its own domain row and
replay it on retry (R-09); kill switches gate route groups, job types and periodic components
with library-owned responses. Two sources feed that one evaluation model:

1. Declared mode (Phase 1; no new infrastructure): values resolved once at startup from the
   application's existing `SettingsSource`, with strict literals, closed-state absence,
   process-kind ownership, retired names and development-only restrictions enforced by the
   library, and value-free diagnostics. A value changes by changing its setting and restarting.
2. Control-plane mode (Phases 2-3; owner-selected scope): an audited PostgreSQL control plane
   whose versioned snapshot a registered Batter component loads and refreshes, so flags and
   switches change without a redeploy; a last-good file for restarts during an outage; a fleet
   view from per-process heartbeats; a small operator CLI with compare-and-set writes; and, in
   Phase 3, push wake-ups, per-subject rollouts and control-plane invariant checks.

Completion signals:

- `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes on Rust 1.98.1 with all new packages, features, examples and
  inventories, and the outcome is recorded in the owning bead.
- The `rollout` facade example demonstrates declared mode, a gated route group, a per-request
  view, a pinned job decision and (with `DATABASE_URL`) the control plane; its DB-free tests run
  in the ordinary matrix.
- The single-facade consumer prints each new marker exactly once against PostgreSQL 18: Phase 1
  (declared catalog resolved, pinned decision stored in row, gated job type deferred) and Phase 2
  (loaded before readiness, held entry kept last good, pinned decision executed, kill switch
  overrode a pin, heartbeat recorded build and version).
- Every ignored PostgreSQL 18 suite the tasks add passes on an explicit `--ignored` run whose
  command and result are recorded on the owning bead; the new `native-runflag-postgres` hosted
  job has a recorded run URL.
- Fresh-agent evaluations 1 and 2 (T-22, T-24) ran against their frozen oracles, with scored
  decisions and logs archived under `docs/evidence/`. An evaluation the owner defers is closed as
  deferred with that decision quoted on the epic, stays labelled proposed and unexecuted, and
  does not count as met.
- ADR-016, the ADR-010 assessment sections, status rows, experimental labels and
  `docs/references.md` entries exist and agree with the shipped API.

## 2. Scope

In scope: everything in §4 (Design) and the tasks in §5, in three phases plus close-out.

Non-goals (recorded so they are not rebuilt by accident):

- Statsig, OpenFeature or any vendor/remote source behind the handles: no public provider trait,
  source adapter or vendor mapping, and no watch-list row (owner decision). runflag-core's
  disclosed `low_level` publication path (§4.1) accepts validated candidates from any caller; it
  is a weaker escape hatch, not a provider interface, and adding a trait or adapter would reopen
  ADR-014's rejection of a generic provider interface
  (`docs/adr/014-reuse-after-two-consumers.md:54-57`).
- Experiment analysis, exposure-based statistics, dashboards, approval workflows, RBAC.
- A second settings system: settings (URLs, secrets, timeouts, pool sizes, `JOBS_*`) stay in
  `batter::settings`; nothing is added to that module (`crates/batter-core/src/settings.rs:3-6`).
- Native Runledger edits (claim-time gating) while `batter-05ci` owns the worker files.
- Executing deployments, drains or stop-writer windows; Batter declares and verifies, it does
  not orchestrate infrastructure.
- Windows; non-Unix fallbacks (ADR-007).
- Committing, pushing or publishing; those need a separate owner instruction.

Constraints: Rust 1.98.1 and `rust-version = "1.98.1"` everywhere; PostgreSQL 18 minimum for
Batter integrations (`docs/integrations.md:12-13`); zero boolean parameters on public APIs
(`clippy.toml:3`, `Cargo.toml:32`); every `.rs` file the plan adds or edits stays ≤ 800 lines
(`.jig/file-budget.toml:3-8,57`); generic scenario names; every new public API passes the
ADR-010 five-question review (`docs/adr/010-agent-only-consumption.md:52-75`); every claim is
tested or labelled unverified; every public hard cut ships `Breaking:` + `Migration:` + shim
decision checked against the public-API diff method; external semantics recorded in
`docs/references.md`.


## Shared rules for every task (plan §5)

Shared rules for every task: claim the task's bead (filed by T-01) before starting; work on a
branch (never on `master` directly); every new public item has rustdoc, an example and its ADR-010
assessment entry; every claim is tested or labelled unverified; test code that reads the process environment
(child-root markers, test database URLs) lives under `tests/` or in a file that only a
`#[cfg(test)]` module declaration loads, never in an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod` block of a
production file, so T-03's scan does not count it (T-06, T-12, T-14, T-15); every new or changed
`.rs` file
stays ≤ 800 lines (`.jig/file-budget.toml`); no boolean parameters; generic scenario names; record
the verification outcome as a bead comment; a task that changes code, a manifest or a script runs
`bash scripts/verify.sh` once on Rust 1.98.1 after its focused checks pass and before its bead
closes (AGENTS.md "Done Means", §6); committing, pushing and publishing still need an
explicit owner request. Parallel lanes add to shared documents (`CHANGELOG.md`,
`docs/guarantees.md`, `docs/status.md`, `docs/adr/010-agent-only-consumption.md`) only under a
task-named entry or subsection and resolve conflicts on rebase.

Hot spots (`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, every member's dependency and feature tables,
`crates/batter/Cargo.toml`, `crates/batter/src/lib.rs`, `scripts/check_facade_features.py`,
`scripts/test_matrix.py`, `scripts/test_parallel_process.py`, `scripts/verify.sh`,
`scripts/test_verify.py`, `scripts/ci_plan.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
`crates/batter/tests/panic_hook_ownership.rs`, AGENTS.md counts) are edited only by T-02, T-03,
T-11, T-17 and T-25. T-02 declares every dependency and feature later tasks use, so any other lane
leaves `Cargo.lock` unchanged (every `--locked` command fails otherwise) and hands a missing edge to
the next owner. No hot-spot case references an item a later task introduces. The task that changes
a count updates every sentence stating it. Other tasks touch their own package and documentation.

## Critical path, owner gates and parallel lanes (plan §5)

Critical path: T-01 → T-02 → T-04 → T-05 → T-12 → T-13 → T-14 → T-15 → T-17 → T-20 → T-21 →
T-25; T-05 → T-06 → {T-08, T-09, T-10} → T-14 is equally long.

Owner gates on that path: ADR-016 acceptance, answers 5 and 9, T-01's dated crates.io check and the
merge of the concurrent TLS work (before T-02); answers 1, 2 and 7 (before T-12 writes its
migration); a push authorization for the hosted `native-runflag-postgres` run (T-17); answer 4
(T-20 runs or closes as excluded).

Parallel lanes: T-03, T-07 and T-18 start right after T-02; T-12 and T-13 run beside T-06..T-11
once T-05 is done; T-08, T-09 and T-10 run together after T-06; T-16 runs beside T-14 and T-15
after T-13; after T-17, T-19 and T-20 run together and T-21 follows T-20; T-22 (after T-11), T-23
and T-24 run beside Phase 3. Forward migrations after T-12 come only from T-13, T-20 and T-21,
which are serialized, so no two tasks claim the same `schema_revision`.

## Owner questions (safe defaults shown; answers recorded on the epic by T-01)

1. Environment scoping of flags. Default: unscoped flags, one schema per environment;
   `environment` stays a heartbeat label. Needed before T-12 writes its migration.
2. Ledger placement. Default: default schema, `flag_` prefix, shared ledger with
   `set_ignore_missing(true)` and vendoring consts. Needed before T-12 writes its migration.
3. `HttpFailure::Disabled` as a permanent hard cut. Default: accept, no shim. Needed before T-07
   merges.
4. Per-subject rollouts in this epic despite 0/3 consumer evidence. Default: include as T-20.
5. Family and binary name `runflag`. Default: as written, provided T-01's dated crates.io check
   finds `runflag`, `runflag-core`, `runflag-postgres`, `runflag-cli` and `batter-flags` available.
   Needed before T-02.
6. Toggle spelling. Default: `ToggleLiterals` chosen per catalog, `TrueFalse` recommended for
   migrated catalogs.
7. Native store dependency. Default: sqlx only, with a native `CommitOutcomeUnknown` type (no
   `batter-sqlx` dependency in the native family). Needed before T-12 writes its migration.
8. Publishing `runflag-cli`. Default: `publish = false` until the release-train record.
9. An in-repo-authored native family (`runflag/`) instead of `crates/` leaves. Default: native family,
   including the 0.1.0 version line and per-package MIT license copies for runflag-core,
   runflag-postgres and runflag-cli, recorded in ADR-016 and an ADR-006 amendment. Needed before
   T-02.
10. ADR-014's reopening condition (one consumer now composes through the lifecycle layer).
    Default: note in ADR-016, propose a separate re-survey bead.

data.text:
Read-only ADR-010 audit at cadb843809e516c7fd903d62025ab372c34c8e01. Current batter-flags adapter modules and postgres/CLI remain scaffolds; catalog implementation is present. No source changes, commits, or implementation of remedies. T-05 is held by another agent; findings below distinguish current API evidence from planned APIs in .agent/plans/flags-control-plane.md (gitignored design file present locally).

1. Current: declaration identity and relationship finalization are fused. builder/kinds.rs:78 requires a previously minted Flag handle; declare consumes the draft. kinds.rs:163 says enum callers should state each direction using requires, but after declaring A then B.requires(A), A is already immutable. Holding both drafts also conflicts on the mutable CatalogBuilder borrow. Hidden phases are identity allocation -> relationship attachment -> catalog validation/seal. Recommend catalog-level typed relationship methods over already-declared handles before consuming build, or explicit consuming definition/constraint phases if needed; no public unvalidated runtime catalog. Reciprocal requires should be representable without expanding into variant-by-variant conflicts. Failure evidence: isolated external rustc probe returns E0599 for a.requires after declare and E0499 for retaining both drafts. No claim that reciprocal logic is impossible to encode by alternative constraints.

2. Current: Draft has Unset -> Set-once -> Invalid states per owners/pinned_by/only_in/absence/flip_discipline/governed_by, but every public setter returns Self and invalidity is delayed to declare. draft.rs:86-147 and tests/catalog_build.rs:setters_may_be_called_once. Owners::Only accepts an empty slice; pinned_by is callable with Owners::All though forbidden. Recommend a compact validated ownership policy (nonempty explicit owners, pin-only readers checked for disjointness) and constructor-owned or consuming single-assignment policies, avoiding a generic parameter for every field. This is construction-time API debt, not an invalid Catalog escaping validation. Executed probe shows repeated absence compiles then returns BuildError::RepeatedCall.

3. Planned T-05/T-14/T-15: snapshot authority transition and freshness must be one owned state machine, not reconstructed from SnapshotStatus. Plan 4.4:505-581 and 4.10:1063-1111. Distinguish Unpublished, Persisted, ControlPlaneConfirmed; schema/load error, loader lifetime, and time-based freshness are separate dimensions. File v100 -> first control-plane v5 is permitted; control-plane v5 -> v4 is rejected; same version/different digest must not renew freshness; held switches retain prior published state including origin. Publish an immutable record containing snapshot, applied head/digest and confirmation evidence atomically; same poll is not cross-thread atomicity for separate snapshot/timestamp writes. Derive diagnostic status/readiness from this record; preserve accepted boot-age and stale-rule policies. These are source-design risks, not executed runtime defects.

4. Planned T-05/T-09: resolve_pinned -> incompatible -> evaluate_unpinned is an implicit transition. Recommend an opaque rejection capability bound to this flag and invocation, consumed to choose fallback/defer; missing legacy/scheduled pins remain separate explicit application choices. Durable row persistence and truth of application provenance remain application obligations; do not claim types prove remote writes.

The transition lacks its required retry timing payload. Represent AwaitingPublication(Recheck) separately from published Released/Tripped policy; use one gate outcome function. T-05 implemented in crates/batter-flags-core on feat/flags-snapshots-jkw6-5 (stacked on PR #81). Nothing is committed or pushed.

DELIVERED
- base.rs: Base/BaseBuilder (resolved literals, recorded absences, revision() and shared_revision()).
- candidate.rs, snapshot.rs: Candidate, CandidateRow, ValidationScope, Snapshot with per-entry holding (HoldCause), counted unknown/not-owned rows, SnapshotRejection for structural corruption only.
- view.rs, view/decide.rs: SnapshotView, the one kill-switch function (floor, stale rule, served state), release/mode layering, governing override, gate_switch, pin and replay.

DECISIONS AND DEVIATIONS FROM THE PLAN (for ADR-016 / P-1 and docs / P-2)
1. Telemetry names follow the batter consolidation, not the plan text: target `batter::flags`, `feature_flag.provider.name` = `batter-flags`, cause attribute `batter.flags.cause`. Consequence: `batter=warn` now filters flag evaluation events (plan 4.13 said it would not); `batter::flags=warn` is the selector. docs/operations must say so.
2. Base/BaseBuilder live in core's `low_level`. The plan put the presence record in batter-flags' Resolved; core needs an input type to compute revisions and mint views. T-06 should wrap Base, not duplicate it. revision() covers every declaration (a non-owned one at its code default or safe state); shared_revision() covers Owners::All. Both are pinned by independent vectors.
3. Handles carry their typed defaults (ReleaseFlag/ModeFlag code_default, KillSwitch safe_state), so evaluation never re-types a default from the catalog.
4. Decision has an `error()` accessor and ErrorCause is the closed vocabulary for events and counts (10 causes, including the pin arms; a Decision never carries a pin arm).
5. Pins record the effective decision: a governed flag whose switch is engaged is pinned at its code default, and a replay still checks the replaying view's governing switch. `pin` is infallible: a handle the view cannot answer for is pinned at its code default and counted and reported as `evaluate` does.
6. Reason omits TargetingMatch and Split (arrive with 4.11). Public enums are exhaustive, so adding them is a recorded breaking change.
7. CandidateRow has no archived marker. The store's load excludes archived rows ("archived keys load as absent"), so a marker would be a state the canonical loader never produces and the digest does not cover. I had added one during implementation and removed it.
8. Layer::Held { since } is the version of the snapshot that last served the state as published, not the row's own updated version (pinned with distinct numbers).
9. SnapshotDigest covers the version and the rows sorted by key (key, kind, value type, updated version, state text exactly as read), held and unknown rows included; archival is not an input.
10. State encoding 1 is decoded by a strict hand-written scanner because serde_json accepts repeated fields. Any member order, JSON whitespace and string escapes are accepted; a repeated, missing, extra or mistyped field is `unknown_row_encoding`. Shared vectors: crates/batter-flags-core/tests/support/state_encoding_1.json (5 writer, 63 reader), reusable by T-12 (writer) and T-15 (file entries).
11. Events: ordinary DEBUG; gate DEBUG released and INFO engaged; an error evaluation WARN the first time per (handle, cause) per Base, DEBUG after, always counted; error.type iff reason is error; semconv v1.45.0 names pinned.
12. `fire` in events.rs is split by level. tracing's `event!` expands larger when the workspace unifies tracing's `log` feature, so a function holding three expansions passed Clippy alone and failed `--workspace`. Per-package Clippy can hide that; verify.sh's workspace run does not.

ADR-010 PROACTIVE INVALID-STATE REVIEW (new public APIs)
- View, Decision, Pinned have private fields and no public constructor except the disclosed low_level path and serde for Pinned; compile_fail doctests cover forging a Decision and a SnapshotView.
- The low_level path cannot tell a complete record from an incomplete one. Caller obligations are now disclosed together in the low_level module docs: record every literal, record absent required settings (an omission serves the variant instead of holding it), carry the replaced snapshot on every load after the first (an omission releases a held engaged switch to its safe state), assert source and freshness truthfully. Each is exercised by a test.
- Residual, by design: a handle from another catalog, or a flag the process kind does not own, compiles and is refused at evaluation (error + count), not at compile time. The canonical enforcement points are T-06 (resolve records every declaration) and T-14 (the loader owns carrying). T-14 should make carrying unforgettable in its own API.

- T-05 is closed but its code is uncommitted on feat/flags-snapshots-jkw6-5 (stacked on PR #81); T-06 needs that branch until it is committed and merged.
Notes from T-05 (batter-jkw6.5), implemented on feat/flags-snapshots-jkw6-5 and not yet merged:
- Reuse core's `low_level::{Base, BaseBuilder}`: Resolved should own a Base (or the BaseBuilder) rather than recompute revisions. `Base::revision()` and `shared_revision()` already match independent golden vectors (crates/batter-flags-core/tests/revisions.rs, including the ("ab","c") versus ("a","bc") framing case), so T-06's revision vectors can assert through Resolved without new framing code.
- `declared::resolve` must record, for every declaration whose setting was present, the literal (`BaseBuilder::flag`/`switch`), and for every enabling variant whose required settings were absent or empty, `settings_absent`. The core cannot detect an omission (see the low_level "Caller obligations" docs); resolve iterating every declaration is what makes it total.
- Telemetry names are `batter::flags` (target), `batter-flags` (provider) and `batter.flags.cause`, not the plan's `runflag` spellings. `Base::error_count(cause)` exposes the per-cause tally for the startup report if wanted.
- Views capture the tracing Dispatch and current Span at construction; build startup and test views inside the dispatcher a test captures.
- TestFlags must wrap `Base::test_view` (Source::Test); never build runtime kill-switch tests on the other constructors.

Note from T-05 (batter-jkw6.5): `Candidate::carrying(&previous)` is how a held kill switch keeps its last published state. It is optional in core's disclosed low_level path, so a loader that forgets it releases a held engaged switch to its safe state. The loader here owns that sequence; make carrying unforgettable in the loader's own API (it holds the served snapshot) and test "held switch keeps its state across loads" end to end. Layer::Held { since } is the version of the snapshot that last served the state, so the loader should carry the snapshot it actually published, not a stored row version. Only a state published from a control-plane candidate counts as last good for persistence (plan 4.4): carry a file-sourced snapshot only for in-process evaluation.

For ADR-016 from T-05 (batter-jkw6.5): record these as decisions, not accidents. (1) The evaluation event target is `batter::flags`, so `batter=warn` filters it and `batter::flags` selects it; this replaces plan 4.13's `runflag=warn` sentence. (2) Layer::Held { since } is the snapshot version that last served the state. (3) Archived keys load as absent: a candidate row has no archived state and the snapshot digest has no archival input. (4) Pins record the effective decision, including a governing override, and `pin` is infallible (a handle the view cannot answer for is pinned at its code default). (5) The held kill switch is the single history-dependent exception to "one (build, version, declared revision) denotes one rule set", and it is the reason Candidate::carrying exists. (6) The ADR-010 residual: a foreign or not-owned handle is refused at evaluation, not at compile time.

For docs from T-05 (batter-jkw6.5): docs/operations (or the rollout example) must say the flag evaluation events use target `batter::flags` (so `batter=warn` filters them), ordinary evaluations are DEBUG, an engaged gate is INFO, and the first error per handle and cause is WARN. docs/testing.md needs the new suites (evaluation, governance, kill_switch, handles, snapshots, revisions, pins, pins_serde, events, event_levels, events_pins, state_encoding) and the ignored `hot_path` micro-benchmark command: `cargo test --release -p batter-flags-core --test hot_path -- --ignored --nocapture`. docs/status.md rows for snapshots, evaluation, pins and events should say Experimental and point at the evidence; the hot-path cost stays labelled unverified.

Note from T-05 (batter-jkw6.5) for this process bead. RUNFLAG_CORE_BARE (`cargo test -p batter-flags-core --no-default-features --locked`) is still undelivered, and nothing in scripts/test_matrix.py builds the bare crate (the all-features workspace run unifies serde on and would hide an unconditional serde use). Thirteen test roots were added; these compile empty without `serde`: tests/pins_serde.rs, events_pins.rs, state_encoding.rs (and T-04's manifest.rs, manifest_decode.rs), so the bare job's count differs from the all-features one by design. test_parallel_process.py pins batch sizes and the command count, which will need the matching update. Single local run, release profile, macOS: roughly 16-19 ns per call with no dispatcher or a filtering one (resolve_pinned about 24-26), and roughly 26-30 ns per call (about 38 for resolve_pinned) when the event is received. The filtered case costing about the same as no dispatcher suggests the per-evaluation scope entry (with_default plus Span::in_scope), not the event itself, dominates; that is a hypothesis for the profile, not a finding.

Follow-up to the ADR-010 audit batter-jkw6.31 (concern 2) and plan Amendment A3, item 2. The catalog relationship phases (concern 1) were settled with T-05; this is the remaining single-assignment policy debt in the T-04 builder surface.

Evidence (reproduced against the built library): every declaration policy setter fills an Option slot and reports a misuse only at `declare()`. These all compile: a repeated `.absence(..)`, `.flip_discipline(..)`, `.owners(..)`, `.only_in(..)` or `.governed_by(..)` (BuildError::RepeatedCall), an empty `Owners::Only(&[])` (EmptyOwners), and `.pinned_by(..)` on a flag every kind owns (PinnedByWithAllOwners). A catalog never escapes invalid; the debt is that known-invalid constructions are expressible.

Design to evaluate, with no generic state parameter per field:
- A validated ownership value replaces `.owners(Owners)` plus `.pinned_by(&[..])`: `Ownership::everyone()` and `Ownership::only([&a, ..])` taking a const-generic array so an empty list does not compile, with `.pinned_by([..])` offered only on the restricted form. Overlap between owners and pin readers, and duplicates, are normalised or refused when the value is built. `Owners` stays as the read-side view that `Declared::owners()` returns.
- Idempotent flag-style setters `.required()` and `.coordinated()` replace `.absence(Absence)` and `.flip_discipline(FlipDiscipline)`, so repeating one is harmless.
- `only_in` and `governed_by` stay set-once with the loud RepeatedCall refusal. A silent last-wins would change an existing declaration during a modification task, so the residual is disclosed in the rustdoc rather than removed.
- Lower priority: `Entry` stores `Kind` beside optional expiry, default, safe state and stale rule, so introspection and manifest conversion coordinate them by hand. A payload enum would keep that internal.

Acceptance: a compile_fail doctest or an impossible construction for each of the three examples above; golden digests and the reference manifest unchanged; the declaration call sites in crates/batter-flags-core tests and docs migrated; the removed errors named in the replacement's rustdoc. Not a published API yet (0.0.1), so no `Breaking:` entry is needed before the first release, but this is cheaper before agents write catalogs than after.

Disposition 2026-11-05, in the working tree on feat/flags-snapshots-jkw6-5 (uncommitted). Each concern was re-verified against the built library first: concern 1 reproduced as E0599 (a requires method after declare) and E0499 (two drafts held at once); concern 2 reproduced as three constructions that compile and fail only at declare(). Settlements are in plan Amendment A3 (section 11).

1. Settled. Relationships are stated on the catalog: CatalogBuilder::{requires, conflicts, both_or_none} over two declared handles, validated eagerly and stored on the first flag named, so a pair is reciprocal in either declaration order. Digests are unchanged: the pinned catalog and mixed-invariant golden vectors pass without edits, and a new test shows declaration order and statement order change no digest. The declaration-level setters are removed. New BuildError::SelfInvariant. Tests: tests/relations.rs, catalog_rules.rs.
2. Not changed here; filed as batter-jkw6.32 with the design (a validated Ownership value taking a const-generic non-empty owner list, idempotent required() and coordinated() setters, set-once RepeatedCall kept for only_in and governed_by with the residual disclosed). The lower-priority Entry payload enum is noted there.
3. Settled in core; the loader and publication record are T-06 and T-14. Added: Snapshot::provenance(), Candidate::from_last_good_file, low_level::Authority::consider returning Transition::{Apply, Confirm, Refuse(Regressed | DigestDrift | FileAfterPublication)}, Transition::renews_freshness (a file publication renews nothing), views that refuse a snapshot read from the other source (ViewError::WrongProvenance), and Snapshot::carried() reporting each held switch's state, since-version and provenance. tests/authority.rs runs the audit's sequence: file v100, first control-plane v5 applied, v4 refused, same version and digest confirms, same version with another digest renews nothing. Not built, by design: the atomic record itself needs a clock type, so A3 binds T-06 and T-14 to publish snapshot, authority and confirmation evidence as one immutable value and derive freshness, readiness and status from it.
4. Settled. PinnedResolution::Incompatible carries PinRefusal, bound to the refusing view and the flag; fall_back_to_live(self) is the only live read after a refusal and dropping it defers. UnpinnedBecause loses PinIncompatible in the plan and keeps ScheduledJob and PayloadPredatesPinning, which are application facts. Tests: tests/pin_refusal.rs, a compile_fail doctest for forging a refusal.
5. Settled in core. low_level::gate_switch returns GateReading::{AwaitingPublication, Open, Tripped}. Before any publication a switch reads AwaitingPublication whatever it would serve, except one engaged by its settings floor, which is the operator's explicit setting and reads Tripped; a published file is a publication. T-09 must take the awaiting Recheck as an explicit constructor argument (WhenTripped::Drop carries none), apply Drop only to Tripped, and split Defer-capable and workflow-step constructors so the invalid pair does not compile; T-08 must say what an HTTP gate answers while awaiting. Tests: tests/gates.rs and the expected reading in each of the 636 kill-switch cells.

Notes posted on batter-jkw6.6, .8, .9, .10, .14 and .15. Residual unchanged: a foreign or not-owned handle is refused at evaluation, not at compile time.

Verification (final tree): bash scripts/verify.sh passed on Rust 1.98.1 (rustc 48a229cea, cargo 797e8a9bc), macOS, local PostgreSQL 18.6; exit 0, all 45 bounded matrix commands status 0, no watchdog or overflow; fmt check, file budget (74 files evaluated, 16 notices, 0 warnings, 0 errors), the four Clippy configurations, six matrix parts, cargo doc --all-features -D warnings and all HTTP smokes; no file was modified after the run started. Post-close change 2026-11-05 from the ADR-010 audit batter-jkw6.31 (plan Amendment A3), in the same uncommitted working tree. T-05's public surface changed in four ways, so the earlier comments describe the pre-audit shape where they differ:
- low_level::gate_switch returns GateReading::{AwaitingPublication, Open, Tripped} instead of a Decision (GateReading::decision() recovers it). The event levels are unchanged.
- PinnedResolution<'v, T> is lifetime-bound and its Incompatible arm carries a PinRefusal (rejection(), fall_back_to_live(self)) instead of a bare PinRejection; PinnedResolution::rejection() reads the arm without consuming it.

The "Caller obligations" in the low_level module docs now say a view's source follows from the snapshot's provenance; the obligation to carry the replaced snapshot and to assert freshness remain. The full scripts/verify.sh was re-run on this tree and passed; evidence is on batter-jkw6.31.

Post-close change 2026-11-05 from the ADR-010 audit batter-jkw6.31 (plan Amendment A3), in the uncommitted T-05 working tree: the declaration-level `requires`, `conflicts` and `both_or_none` are removed from ReleaseDeclaration, ModeDeclaration and the toggle impls, and replaced by CatalogBuilder::{requires, conflicts, both_or_none} taking two declared handles, because a relationship needs both handles and a declaration is consumed by declare(), so the flag declared first could never state its side of a reciprocal pair. The stored invariants, catalog digest and manifest are byte-identical (the pinned vectors pass unchanged). PR #81 still has the old setters; the change reaches the branch with the T-05 commit, or can be applied to the PR separately. New refusal: BuildError::SelfInvariant. The single-assignment setter debt (concern 2 of the audit) is batter-jkw6.32.

Plan Amendment A3 (ADR-010 audit batter-jkw6.31), item 5: the reader this task builds publishes through a `watch`, so the record it publishes is settled here, not in T-14. Publish one immutable record, never a bare `Arc<Snapshot>` beside a separately written timestamp: the snapshot, its `low_level::Authority` and the confirmation evidence (a Tokio instant) together. Freshness, readiness and status are derived from that one record at capture. Two writes (publish, then record the confirmation) are not one atomic publication across threads: a view captured between them pairs a new snapshot with an old confirmation and can read Stale, engaging an `EngageWhenStale` switch for an instant. Core already supplies the pure part (`Snapshot::provenance()`, `Candidate::from_last_good_file`, `Authority::consider`), and `Base::control_plane_view` and `persisted_file_view` now refuse a snapshot read from the other source, so build each view from the matching provenance. `TestFlags` wraps `Base::test_view`, which accepts either.

Plan Amendment A3 (ADR-010 audit batter-jkw6.31), item 3: `low_level::gate_switch` now returns `GateReading::{AwaitingPublication, Open, Tripped}`, not a bare decision. Before any publication every switch reads AwaitingPublication whatever it would serve, except one engaged by its settings floor (the operator's explicit setting), which reads Tripped. The plan never said what an HTTP gate answers in that window. Decide it explicitly in the gate builder, with an exhaustive `match` and no wildcard so a new reading cannot be forgotten; the choice (for example the sanitized disabled response while awaiting, or serving) should follow the `LoadPolicy`, and HTTP admission already stays closed under `unready_until_loaded` until a control-plane read is published (plan 4.10), so the open question is the `start_on_defaults` window after a failed first attempt. The gate event level is unchanged: INFO while the decision is engaged, DEBUG otherwise.

Plan Amendment A3 (ADR-010 audit batter-jkw6.31), items 3 and 4, for the job wrappers:
1. Gate states. `gate_switch` returns `GateReading::{AwaitingPublication, Open, Tripped}`. `GatedHandler` matches it exhaustively: Open runs, Tripped applies the declared `WhenTripped`, AwaitingPublication is always `DeferAttempt` with a `Recheck`. `WhenTripped::Drop` carries no `Recheck`, so the old rule "Drop acts as DeferAttempt before publication" had no retry timing to apply. Take the awaiting recheck as an explicit constructor argument (`GatePolicy { when_tripped, awaiting: Recheck }`), and apply `Drop` only to Tripped, so missing initial data can never become a drop. Test: no publication plus Drop never drops and defers with a validated recheck.
2. Constructors. Replace the runtime refusal of `Defer` with `MayRunAsWorkflowStep` by two constructors: `gated_direct` taking `DirectWhenTripped::{Defer, DeferAttempt, Drop}` and `gated_workflow_step` taking `StepWhenTripped::{DeferAttempt, Drop}`, so the invalid pair does not compile. That a type is only ever enqueued directly stays the application's assertion; the native workflow dead-letter on a misused Defer is a native contract this task can only document.
3. Pins.
